headline: Dr. Smith reviewed your blood tests and recommended starting atorvastatin for high cholesterol and vitamin D for a low vitamin D level.

followUps.title: Start atorvastatin
followUps.detail: Take one 20 mg tablet once a day at bedtime.

followUps.title: Buy vitamin D3
followUps.detail: You can buy it without a prescription. Look for a bottle that says 1,000 IU (international units) or 25 micrograms.

followUps.title: Book your cholesterol and liver blood tests
followUps.detail: Book the blood draw at the front desk. Get it done in early September rather than waiting for your blood pressure visit.

followUps.title: Keep your blood pressure visit
followUps.detail: Your September visit with Dr. Smith is still planned.

instructions.text: Take vitamin D3, 1,000 IU once a day with a meal.
If you get muscle pain or weakness you can’t explain, call Dr. Smith before stopping atorvastatin.
Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice while taking atorvastatin. A little grapefruit now and then is fine.

unchanged.text: Keep taking ramipril 10 mg once a day in the morning.
Keep taking amlodipine 10 mg once a day.
Keep using acetaminophen as needed for your knee.

openQuestions.text: Is low vitamin D part of why you feel tired? Dr. Smith said it might be a small part of the reason.
Will you need atorvastatin forever? Dr. Smith said you’ll most likely take it long term.
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: As long as you’re doing well on it.
